name: יְרֹחָם
gloss: he is shown compassion; or may he be shown compassion
summary: Seven men: the Levite father of Elkanah and grandfather of Samuel (1Sa 1:1; 1Ch 6:12, 19); a Benjamite whose sons lived in Jerusalem (1Ch 8:27), and the father of Ibneiah (1Ch 9:8); a priest, father of Adaiah (1Ch 9:12; Neh 11:12); the father of Joelah and Zebadiah of Gedor, who came to David at Ziklag (1Ch 12:8); the father of Azarel, commander of Dan (1Ch 27:22); and the father of Azariah, a commander of hundreds with Jehoiada (2Ch 23:1). The name has the consonants and nearly the vowels of the pual imperfect יְרֻחָם, “he will be shown compassion”, used of the one who confesses and forsakes his sin (Pro 28:13) and the fatherless (Hos 14:4); scripture does not explain the name.

evidence.note: Elkanah “son of יְרֹחָם, son of Elihu”.
“Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham of Gedor.”
“He who confesses and forsakes them יְרֻחָם, will be shown compassion”: the same consonants as the name.

note: Takes t.bz.aj (10 tokens) and j.dk.ag, a zero-token cross-reference whose word is יְרֹחָם though BDB's gloss points to יְרַחְמְאֵל. TIPNR's Jeroham@1Ch.12.7 is 1Ch 12:8 in the Hebrew numbering; Jeroham@1Sa.1.1 covers 1Ch 6:12, 19 (Eng. 6:27, 34) and Jeroham@1Ch.9.12 covers Neh 11:12. The vowel ō for the pual's u is not explained; the reading “may he be shown compassion” takes it as a wish, as Jerahmeel “may God have compassion”.
